---
The sky appears blue because of Rayleigh scattering, where molecules of air scatter sunlight in all directions. Since shorter wavelengths of light, like blue, are scattered more efficiently than longer wavelengths like red, the scattered blue light dominates our view of the sky. When we look at the sky, we see the scattered blue photons that have been deflected toward us, while the other colors are either absorbed or pass through less visibly.
